answer_1.quote: We explore the open and closed-source LLMs space to sample the current landscape of available models and evaluate them on the following sequence-to-sequence tasks, reframed as text generation tasks without the requirement for task-specific fine-tuning: text summarisation, text simplification, and grammatical error correction (GEC).
answer_1.outputs: Generated summaries for summarisation, simplified texts for simplification, and corrected sentences for grammatical error correction

answer_2.quote: We used the most widely adopted reference-based metrics for each of the tasks.

answer_3.quote: We used GPT-4 as an additional reviewer to assess whether it can be reliably deployed in place of human reviewers.

answer_4.quote: Due to budgetary and time constraints, we recruited 3 human reviewers through the Prolific platform
answer_4.guideline: Evaluators scored outputs based on defined criteria: for summarisation (Relevance, Fluency, Coherence, Consistency on a 5-point Likert scale), simplification (Semantics, Fluency, Simplicity on a 5-point Likert scale), and GEC (Semantics, Grammaticality, Over-correction with specific scales).
